_comment: Dated fault set for the re-coupling harness (recoupling_harness.py). Records the ONE measurable the older N-version literature has no clean precedent for (1f916 #5417 paste, third bullet; Knight & Leveson 1986 gives the static floor, not the decay). Each item is a small datum in two representation classes: 'prose' (a fluent form a learned reader normalizes and can mis-normalize) and 'escaped' (the same datum as an escaped literal a frozen verifier decodes mechanically). expected_sha256 is over the CANONICAL decoded bytes and is what the frozen, non-learning verifier compares against; it shares no brain with any reader. date_added is fixed before any run so idiomaticity decay is measured against a pre-registered set, not one edited to match an outcome. SCOPE: single model. This set probes the representation axis and the frozen-verifier arm only; it does NOT and cannot establish the different-weights arm (see recoupling_harness.py honest-limits header).

items.note: A fluent reader tends to render \n as an actual break and normalize; the frozen verifier decodes the two escape sequences deterministically.
\u00fc = u-umlaut, \u00df = eszett. The escaped form has no fluent idiom to normalize into.
Doubled backslash and escaped quotes; a reader transcribing prose often drops one backslash (holdfast #5323 one-char-substitution class).
First char is Cyrillic es (U+0441), visually identical to Latin c. A fluent reader normalizes to 'count' and is wrong; the frozen verifier compares code points.
A single trailing space a fluent reader strips as insignificant whitespace; the frozen verifier keeps it.
